title: GRS JSON document
description:
Terms:
GRS is GoodRelax Scheduler, which opens and edits a Schedule Document and reads and writes GRS JSON files, the format that this GRS JSON Schema defines.
MSPDI (Microsoft Project XML Data Interchange) is the XML file format that Microsoft Project uses. GRS can also read and write MSPDI (.xml) files.
A key inside an MSPDI object (project, calendars, tasks, resources, assignments and their parts) has the meaning and values of the MSPDI element of the same name; only grs, parentTaskUid and siblingIndex are GRS's own, and a description notes what GRS does differently.
Concepts:
WBS is the tree of parent and child tasks, as in MSPDI.
Task groups are GRS's own objects that let GRS draw several tasks in one Task Group Lane. Each task names exactly one task group in grs.taskGroupId.
An MSPDI object keeps the values that only GRS uses under the key grs of that object.
GRS counts working days using a single calendar: the calendar that project.calendarUid names.
Passthrough: GRS keeps the MSPDI values that GRS does not use in grs.passthrough of each object, and the MSPDI elements that GRS does not turn into objects in the passthrough lists; GRS writes both back to MSPDI.
Actual dates are the authoritative source of task progress. GRS decides from the actual dates of a task, together with resume and resumeValid, whether the task is not started, in progress, suspended, or finished. GRS recalculates percentComplete from those dates when GRS opens a GRS JSON file.
Delay Diagnostics: GRS never stores Delay Diagnostics results in a GRS JSON file, because a stored result goes out of date as soon as the Schedule Document changes.
The shape of GRS JSON:
$schema           Address of this schema
schemaVersionUtc  Version of the shape
buildVersionUtc   GRS build that wrote the file
documentStamp     Last change, last save and last editor
documentSettings  How GRS shows the schedule on opening
scheduleData      Schedule data
  +- head values: scheduleDataTimeZone, sourceFormat, importedTopTaskOutlineLevel, mspdiImportCount, lastMspdiImport, highestIssuedUid
  +- same as MSPDI: project, calendars, tasks, resources, assignments
  +- passthrough lists: passthroughCalendars, passthroughTasks, passthroughResources, passthroughAssignments
  +- GRS only: taskGroups, baselineTasks, highlightBoxes, commentBoxes
changeLogEntries  Notes on changes
Omit a property that has no value: never write null or [].

$schema.title: Address of this schema
$schema.description: The address of the latest GRS schema; every document holds the same address.

schemaVersionUtc.title: Version of the shape
schemaVersionUtc.description: The UTC time when the shape of GRS JSON, meaning the keys and the rules, last changed.

buildVersionUtc.description: This value serves debugging only; schemaVersionUtc tells whether GRS can read the file.
buildVersionUtc.title: GRS build that wrote the file

documentStamp.title: Last change, last save and last editor

documentSettings.title: How GRS shows the schedule on opening
documentSettings.description: GRS writes the keys from the widest effect to the narrowest.

displayScaleRatio.description: GRS multiplies the values of keys ending in Px, which are CSS pixels, by this ratio when drawing, and saves those values unscaled.

fontSizePreset.description: GRS holds the pixel size of each step, and displayScaleRatio scales that size.

isThemeMonochrome.description: This value changes only the drawing; the colors saved in the Schedule Document stay the same.

themeHue.description: GRS holds the hue angle of each name.

viewTimeZone.description: The Display Base Time Zone: the time zone in which GRS shows date-times on the Schedule Canvas and the Time Ruler.

type.description: "sameAsScheduleData": GRS shows date-times in the time zone of scheduleData.scheduleDataTimeZone and follows that time zone when the time zone changes.

utcOffset.description: The offset already includes any daylight saving time, and GRS uses the offset all year.

zoneNameType.description: Which name of the zone GRS shows for this clock: the standard-time name or the daylight-time name. This value does not change the offset.

dayWidthPx.description: The Day Width (the horizontal zoom): the width of one calendar day on the Time Ruler.

fitDayRange.description: The Fit Span: the days that Zoom to Fit and PNG and SVG pictures show.

type.description: "fixed": the Fit Span runs from firstDay to lastDay with no margin. "automatic": the Fit Span covers everything that GRS draws, plus a margin that GRS fixes and does not save.

firstDay.description: Write this key only when type is "fixed". The first day of the Fit Span, as a day in the Display Base Time Zone.

verticalZoom.description: When this key is absent, GRS chooses both values as Zoom to Fit does; when only automaticallyShownDepth is absent, GRS chooses that value as Zoom to Fit does.

ratio.description: The vertical size of the Task Graphics as a ratio to the default size.

automaticallyShownDepth.description: The depth to which GRS shows task groups with showMode "automatic".

isTaskGroupPanelWidthFixed.description: true: taskGroupPanelWidthPx sets the width of the Task Group Panel and the Panel Divider stays fixed; false: a drag of the Panel Divider changes taskGroupPanelWidthPx.

pinnedTaskGroupIds.description: The ids of the Pinned Task Groups.

taskPlacementDirection.description: The Placement Direction: how GRS stacks the overlapping tasks of one Task Group Lane on Stack Tiers; this value does not order the task groups.

type.description: "automatic": nobody has chosen a place, so GRS chooses one on opening; this value does not mean today or the status date.

leftEdgeDay.description: Write this key only when type is "fixed". The day at the left edge of the view, as a day in the time zone of scheduleData.scheduleDataTimeZone.

leftEdgeDayOffsetPercent.description: Only when type is "fixed". How far the left edge lies to the right of the start of leftEdgeDay, in percent of one day.

topEdgeTaskGroupId.description: Write this key only when type is "fixed". The id of the task group at the top edge of the view. When that task group no longer exists, GRS treats the scroll position as "automatic".

topEdgeTaskGroupOffsetPercent.description: Only when type is "fixed". How far the top edge lies below the top of that task group, not of the screen, in percent of the lane height plus the gap below.

scheduleCanvasElements.description: GRS writes the keys in this order: bars, labels, lines.

isProgressStatusMarkVisible.description: When this value is true, GRS draws the Resume Marks and the Progress Status Marks.

isProgressLineVisible.description: GRS draws the Progress Line when this value is true.

parentTaskProgressToleranceWorkingDays.description: The working days by which a parent's progress point may stray beyond the progress points below before Delay Diagnostics marks the parent doubtful.

tableWindows.description: The checks, column filters and sort of the tables in the Search Window, the Delay Diagnostics Report Window and the Resource List Window, but no window positions.

searchWindow.description: The table settings of the Search Window, which shows the task table or the Comment Box table, one at a time. columnFilters holds the filters of both tables, told apart by column; columnSort holds one sort, on a column of either table. The checks belong to the task table only.

importedTopTaskOutlineLevel.description: The MSPDI OutlineLevel of the top tasks in the imported file, not counting the project summary task; GRS gives this OutlineLevel to the top WBS tasks when writing MSPDI.

lastMspdiImport.description: People and AI agents read this object; GRS compares mspdiImportCount instead.

fileName.description: GRS writes the file name only, never the folder, so that the file keeps no personal path.

highestIssuedUid.description: The highest uid that GRS has issued, one counter for tasks, resources, assignments and calendars. When the key is absent, GRS takes the highest uid of the four lists on opening.

project.description: scheduleData.project holds only the values for the whole project: the MSPDI lists (calendars, tasks, resources, assignments) sit beside project in scheduleData, not inside project as in MSPDI.

calendars.description: GRS keeps the calendars other than the one that project.calendarUid names only to write them back to MSPDI.

precedingCalendarUid.description: The uid of the nearest calendar in calendars[] that precedes this element in MSPDI. No key puts the element first; equal values keep array order.

tasks.description: The order of this list carries no meaning: parentTaskUid and siblingIndex give the WBS tree.

passthroughTasks.description: The whole MSPDI Task elements outside tasks[], such as the project summary task.

precedingTaskUid.description: The uid of the nearest task in tasks[] that precedes this element in MSPDI. No key puts the element first; equal values keep array order.

precedingResourceUid.description: The uid of the nearest resource in resources[] that precedes this element in MSPDI. No key puts the element first; equal values keep array order.

precedingAssignmentUid.description: The uid of the nearest assignment in assignments[] that precedes this element in MSPDI. No key puts the element first; equal values keep array order.

taskGroups.description: The task groups, depth first, as a tree of drawing rows separate from the WBS.

baselineTasks.description: The baseline, a saved copy of earlier task dates. Baseline tasks hold no shape: each Baseline Outline takes the shape of the current task with the same uid.

highlightBoxes.description: The Highlight Boxes: rectangles in the Task Group Lanes that mark a range of days over a range of task groups.

commentBoxes.description: The Comment Boxes in the Task Group Lanes. The Leader Line of each Comment Box points at a task, a Highlight Box or a free point.

changeLogEntries.title: Notes on changes
changeLogEntries.description: The Change Log: notes that people or an AI write about changes to the Schedule Document, oldest first.

Project.description: GRS writes the keys in the order of the MSPDI schema, and the GRS part comes last under grs.

creationDate.description: GRS writes the moment of creation when GRS makes a new Schedule Document.

calendarUid.description: When this key is absent or matches no uid in calendars[], GRS uses the first calendar with isBaseCalendar true, or else a built-in Monday-to-Friday calendar.

defaultStartTime.description: GRS gives this time of day to a start that GRS sets by the day, and uses 08:00:00 when the key is absent.

defaultFinishTime.description: GRS gives this time of day to a finish that GRS sets by the day and to a milestone start, and uses 17:00:00 when the key is absent.

minutesPerDay.description: GRS uses 480 when the key is absent, and warns on opening when the working times of a day total otherwise.

weekStartDay.description: Sunday is 0 here but 1 in calendars[].weekDays[].dayType.

baseCalendarUid.description: GRS writes this value back but does not inherit: GRS counts only the days that this calendar lists.

workingTimes.description: On a working day without workingTimes, GRS uses 08:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00. On a non-working day, GRS keeps workingTimes for MSPDI and counts no working time.

Exception.description: GRS keeps an exception without fromDate or toDate for MSPDI and leaves it out of the count.

fromDate.description: GRS reads only the date, and GRS writes T00:00:00 when GRS sets the date.

toDate.description: GRS reads only the date, so T00:00:00 still counts the whole day; GRS writes T23:59:00.

type.description: GRS counts working days with a one-off exception only, which covers every day from fromDate to toDate: type 9, no type, or type 1 (every day) with period 1 or no period. GRS keeps the other exceptions unchanged and leaves them out of the count.

workingTimes.description: On a working exception, these spans replace the spans of the day of the week; a working exception without workingTimes uses 08:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00. On a non-working exception, GRS keeps workingTimes for MSPDI and counts no working time.

WorkingTime.description: GRS refuses overlapping spans in one day and spans that do not start before they end (a toTime of 00:00:00 counts as 24:00); touching spans are fine.

toTime.description: 00:00:00 means 24:00, the end of the day.

Task.description: GRS decides the progress status by these checks in order, and the first match wins: no actualStart, not started; actualFinish present, finished; resumeValid false, suspended with no resume date; resume present, suspended with a resume date; otherwise in progress.

finish.description: A milestone has the same start and finish.

resumeValid.description: Only a written false marks a suspension with no resume date. GRS writes true with each resume date.

percentComplete.description: Actual working time (actualStart to actualFinish or stop) over planned working time, times 100, rounded, uncapped. Without planned working time, the value is 100 after actualFinish, else 0. A task with actualStart and neither actualFinish nor stop counts 0 actual working time.

actualFinish.description: A percentComplete of 100 does not mean finished.

calendarUid.description: GRS keeps this value only to write it back to MSPDI.

siblingIndex.description: GRS writes 0, 1, 2 without gaps, reads the smallest first, and keeps array order on ties; siblings without siblingIndex follow, in array order.

startSlopeCalendarDays.description: The Start Slope in calendar days: GRS slants the start edge of the Plan Bar inward, from start toward finish, to mark a start that is not firm, without changing the schedule.

finishSlopeCalendarDays.description: The Finish Slope in calendar days: GRS slants the finish edge of the Plan Bar inward, from finish toward start, to mark a finish that is not firm, without changing the schedule.

importOrigin.description: A task made in GRS has no importOrigin.

linkLag.description: The lag in tenths of a minute, whatever lagFormat says: 4800 is 480 minutes, one working day when project.minutesPerDay is 480.

lagFormat.description: GRS counts the lag only for 3, 5 and 7. When lagFormat is absent, GRS leaves the lag out of the count.

ImportOrigin.description: Which MSPDI file and task an imported task came from.

sourceTaskUid.description: The value can differ from uid, because GRS may give the imported task a new uid.

importSessionId.description: This id stands in for sourceProjectUid when the MSPDI file had no Project UID.

mspdiImportCountWhenLastIncluded.description: A copy of scheduleData.mspdiImportCount at the last import whose file contained this task. A value below the current count means that the latest import left this task out.

type.description: Every resource has the same keys, whatever the code.

calendarUid.description: GRS keeps this value only to write it back to MSPDI.

TaskGroup.description: A task group: one Task Group Lane and one row of the Task Group Panel.

name.description: When the key is absent, GRS shows an empty title.

parentTaskGroupId.description: When the key is absent, the task group is a top-level task group (depth 1).

siblingIndex.description: GRS lists the task groups from the smallest value at the top; task groups without siblingIndex follow, in array order.

style.description: When style is absent, GRS leaves the Task Group Lane uncolored.

minHeightPx.description: Vertical zoom leaves this minimum unchanged.

representativeTaskUid.description: The uid of the WBS task that this task group stands for.

hyperlink.description: The title of the task group link, not the address.

showMode.description: What a person wants for this task group. "shown": GRS draws the task group at any depth unless an ancestor hides the task group. "hidden": GRS hides the task group and every task group below. "automatic": GRS decides from automaticallyShownDepth, the pins and the path to a shown task group below. "hiddenUntilZoomIn": GRS hides the task group and every task group below until the next vertical zoom-in.

allowedEditorGroupName.description: The name of the group of people allowed to edit the tasks in this task group. GRS treats those tasks as read-only for every person and AI agent, because GRS alone holds no group of its own.

firstDay.description: The first day that the Highlight Box covers, as a day in the time zone of scheduleData.scheduleDataTimeZone.

firstTaskGroupId.description: The box covers every task group through lastTaskGroupId in task group tree order, both ends included.

CommentBox.description: One Comment Box: a text box with a Leader Line, whose end (the Leader Anchor) stands at a free point, a task or a Highlight Box.

leaderTarget.description: When the file names a target that the Schedule Data lacks, GRS draws no Leader Line.

bodyOffsetPx.description: The offset from the Leader Anchor to the lower-left corner of the Comment Box body; horizontal and vertical zoom leave this offset unchanged.

dy.description: A positive value moves the box down.

hyperlink.description: The title of the Comment Box link, not the address.

taskGroupTopOffsetPercent.description: Only when type is "freePoint". How far the Leader Anchor lies below the top edge of that Task Group Lane, in percent of the lane height.

snapPart.description: Only when type is "task". "milestoneMark" on a milestone, "planBar" or "actualBar" on other tasks.

scheduleDataUpdatedAt.description: A change of documentSettings alone does not move this time.

documentUpdatedAt.description: The last change of the Schedule Document, documentSettings included.

fileSavedAt.description: The key is absent until the first save.

type.description: "template": nobody has edited yet, so the Schedule Document is still the template that comes with GRS.

name.description: The name of the editor: for "agent", the name that the AI reports; for "user", the name of the person, only when GRS knows the name.

changedAt.description: GRS fills in the time when GRS adds the entry; a person may change the time later.

name.description: The name of the editor: the name that a person typed, or the name that an AI reported.

Uid.description: The identifier of a task, a resource, an assignment or a calendar, unique within one array, the same as MSPDI UID, whether the entity came from MSPDI or GRS made the entity; GRS never reuses a uid.

Uuid.description: GRS uses a UUID as the id of an object that only GRS defines, so that objects made apart never share an id; GRS writes the UUID in lower case.

Day.description: A date without a time of day, in the time zone that each key names where that matters. A range of days (firstDay to lastDay) includes both ends.

Time.description: A time of day from 00:00:00 to 23:59:59.

DateTime.description: A local date and time in scheduleData.scheduleDataTimeZone with no offset, as MSPDI writes a date-time. GRS reads the value to the minute and ignores the seconds.

StandardUtcOffset.description: GRS uses the offset all year and never adds daylight saving time.

MspdiValue.description: One MSPDI value: a string that keeps the MSPDI text as written for a text-only element (a boolean stays "0" or "1", a number stays as spelled), an array for a repeatable element (even with one item), or an object keyed by child element names.

Passthrough.description: The MSPDI child elements of one entity that GRS does not use, keyed by element name. GRS writes them back to MSPDI.

MspdiElement.description: One whole MSPDI element that GRS does not hold as an entity, keyed by child element names.

isCalculatedFromOppositeColorScheme.description: A mark on a side that GRS calculated from the opposite side, as a record of origin and not a switch.

type.description: "theme": GRS takes the theme color for the place that holds this color, in the hue of documentSettings.themeHue. With "custom", GRS calculates a side that light or dark lacks from the other side.

name.description: Only when type is "palette". Each name says how the color looks in the light theme; in the dark theme GRS keeps the hue and inverts the lightness.

widthPx.description: Horizontal and vertical zoom leave this width unchanged.

stroke.description: When the key is absent, GRS draws no outline.

taskShape.description: The shape of the Plan Bar and the Actual Bar of a task that is not a milestone. "dumbbell": a thin line with a dot at each end.

fill.description: The fill of the Plan Bar, or of the Milestone Mark for a milestone. No key means no fill.

stroke.description: The outline of the Plan Bar and the Actual Bar, or of the Milestone Mark for a milestone.
When the key is absent, GRS draws no outline and no Leader Line.

sizePx.description: Horizontal and vertical zoom leave this size unchanged.

type.description: An absent firstDay or lastDay leaves that end open.

column.description: The same name means the same content in every table. Search Window, task table: "progressStatus", "percentComplete", "taskType", "taskName", "resourceNames", "start", "finish", "actualStart", "actualFinish", "taskGroupPath" (the path from the top level). Search Window, Comment Box table: "text", "taskGroupName" (the task group of the Leader Anchor), "leaderTargetDay" (the day of the Leader Anchor).

hiddenValues.description: Only when type is "values". The values whose rows the filter hides: the status key listed below for a status column, and the cell text as the table shows the text for any other column. "progressStatus": "notStarted", "inProgress", "suspendedWithResumeDate", "suspendedWithoutResumeDate", "finished", "delay", and, while GRS shows Delay Diagnostics results, the diagnosis marks "unreliable", "bottleneck", "bottleneckPath"; "diagnosisStatus": "unreliable", "suspicion", "omission", "bottleneck", "bottleneckPath", "delay", "finishedDelayContribution"; "taskType": "task", "milestone"; "resourceSelectionStatus": "selected", "notSelected".

firstDay.description: Only when type is "dateRange". The first day that the filter keeps, as a day in the time zone of scheduleData.scheduleDataTimeZone.

isScheduleFilteredByChecks.description: Filter Schedule by Checks, on or off: when true, GRS draws on the Schedule Canvas only the tasks checked in this table.

columnFilters.description: The column filters of this table, one for each filtered column.

isScheduleFilteredByChecks.description: Filter Schedule by Checks, on or off: when true, GRS draws on the Schedule Canvas only the tasks of checked resources, plus unassigned tasks when isUnassignedChecked is true.

columnFilters.description: The column filters of this table, one for each filtered column.
